en: Jose Rizal built a water dam in Dapitan to provide clean drinking water and prevent waterborne diseases among the locals.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm and safe in areas without electricity.
Republic Act 9003 mandates proper household waste segregation to prevent clogged drains and reduce the spread of dengue fever.
Drinking plenty of water and wearing hats during the sunny Sinulog festival prevents heatstroke and severe dehydration.
The Ifugao people traditionally cultivate diverse sweet potato varieties, which provide essential dietary fiber and vitamins for good digestion.
Planting the national tree, Narra, provides thick shade that lowers local temperatures and protects skin from harmful ultraviolet rays.
National Scientist Dr. Alfredo Santos isolated antimicrobial compounds from local plants to develop safe, natural treatments for bacterial infections.
Republic Act 10121 mandates all Philippine schools to conduct regular earthquake and fire drills to ensure student safety during disasters.
The Filipino value of bayanihan helps communities safely evacuate neighbors and share clean drinking water during dangerous typhoons.
Igorot elders use crushed yerba buena leaves as a safe, natural remedy to relieve minor stomachaches and headaches.
Practicing the national martial art, Arnis, requires wearing protective headgear and chest guards to safely prevent concussions and bodily injuries.
Learning basic first-aid terms in your local dialect helps you quickly and accurately communicate injuries to emergency responders.
